title: perf(console): stop the eager stylesheet scanning test files (objectui#6379)
body:
Part of #6379.

Deliberately **not** `Fixes`. This closes one measurable face of that card and leaves its actual question open: merging this must not close it. What remains open is stated under "What this does not do".

## What this does

`apps/console/src/index.css` declares 27 `@source` path globs across `packages/**` plus its own tree, and carried **no `@source not` line at all** — while reaching further than any other source-declaring entry in this repo. Tailwind v4 scans source TEXT, not an import graph, so every test file under those globs was a source for the render-blocking `index-*.css` the console serves: **2373** test files in the packages it names, plus this app's own.

`packages/components/src/index.css` (objectui#8446, objectui#9569) and `packages/runner/src/index.css` (objectui#8454) already carried the exclusion. This entry was the gap — and it is the one whose output is render-blocking.

Two repository-root-anchored `@source not` lines close it. That anchor is the one base covering **both** trees this entry scans: the package globs, and Tailwind's automatic detection root, which is the process CWD — here `apps/console`, where the build runs.

## Evidence

**Class-set diff** — every disappearing class accounted for. 19 classes leave the compiled sheet, and all 19 were traced to test files. The diff is measured on a build that still scans every shipped file, so anything a shipped file genuinely emits survives by construction:

- `prose-lg`, `prose-slate` — 10,302 unminified bytes between them; the typography plugin emits a very large rule block per `prose-*` variant.
- `mt-[3.7331px]` — the self-hosted sentinel of components' own `index-css-scan-excludes-tests.test.ts`: a token that exists **only** to prove that package's exclusion works, which this app was shipping to users.
- `row-1`, `row-42`, `tab-1`, `zoom-10`, `top-200`, `m-9`, `order-1`, `bg-none`, `md:p-3`, `mt-[3.7331px]`, `bg-[color:var(--brand)]`, `flex-grow`, `h-[125px]`, `w-[250px]`, `[group:1]`, `pl-44`, `m-1` — each traced to a `*.test.*` or `__tests__/` file.
- Near-misses checked by hand, all substring artifacts of the grep rather than real uses: `m-1` inside `before:bottom-1`; `flex-grow`/`h-[125px]`/`w-[250px]` inside runner's own comment listing the classes **it** excludes. `pl-44` is the instructive one — the shipped `KanbanImpl.tsx` emits `sm:pl-44` (which survives), the bare `pl-44` came from a test.
- Reverse direction is empty: no class is **added**.

**Positive control** — a negative-only result would also be produced by a scan that found nothing. A marker class injected into a shipped file (`packages/components/src/ui/button.tsx`) still compiles under the new lines; the file was restored and its blob hash re-verified against `HEAD`.

**Ablation** — deleting the two lines turns the new pin test red on both sentinels (`6379.0731px`, own tree; `3.7331px`, another package's tree), confirming it can fail. Restored, hash re-verified.

**Sizes** — built, minified `index-*.css`:

| | raw | gzipped |
|---|---|---|
| before | 365,214 | 47,482 |
| after | 357,216 | 46,527 |
| delta | -7,998 (-2.19%) | -955 (-2.00%) |

**First contentful paint** — production build, served locally with boot endpoints mocked and gzip on, Playwright, cache disabled, fresh context per run, **median of 7 runs** per cell:

| profile | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| localhost, no throttling | 64 ms | 76 ms |
| 20 Mbps / 80 ms RTT | 288 ms | 292 ms |
| Fast 4G (4 Mbps / 70 ms) | 688 ms | 688 ms |

**FCP does not move.** 955 gzipped bytes is under 2 ms of transfer at 4 Mbps, below this measurement's resolution. Reported as measured rather than rounded into a win.

The card's attribution does reproduce: FCP lands ~22 ms after the last stylesheet finishes at every profile (Fast 4G: last stylesheet 665.8 ms, FCP 688 ms), so first paint really is gated on the render-blocking CSS.

**Negative control — a scan-surface change deliberately NOT made.** This entry opens with a bare `@import 'tailwindcss'`, so automatic source detection is ON, and the sibling packages carry `source(none)`. Adding it here looks like the obvious next step. Measured: automatic detection contributes **exactly one** class beyond the explicit globs (`w-100`, 54 bytes, sourced from a doc under `apps/console/docs/`). Excluding this app's 170 KB `CHANGELOG.md` — the objectui#9569 hazard — changes the compiled sheet by **zero bytes**. So `source(none)` buys nothing here and risks dropping a class for no measured gain; it is not in this diff.

## What this does not do

It does not shorten first paint, and it is not the fix for #6379. That card's three routes were carved up by triage: route 3 (shrink the sheet if its scan surface is wider than the eager route needs) is the only one needing no product ruling, and this is route 3, carried out and measured. The measurement says route 3's ceiling is ~2% of the render-blocking CSS.

The remaining ~690 ms on Fast 4G is the sheet the app genuinely needs. Reaching it requires route 1 (make the app CSS non-blocking) or route 2 (inline a critical subset) — both of which change what an unstyled first frame is allowed to look like, or need a rule for what counts as critical. Those are product rulings and are **not** touched here. #6379 stays open for them.

The 27 package globs were **not** narrowed. "This plugin is not on the eager route" is a fact about the JS closure; whether an eager component renders its classes is a separate question, and dropping a glob would silently unstyle a lazily-loaded plugin. No measurement here supports it.

## Gates run

`build` · `type-check` · `lint` (0 errors; the new file adds 0 of the 212 pre-existing warnings) · full `@object-ui/console` suite (101 files, 1158 tests) · `check:control-bytes` · `check:new-line-citations` · `check:eager-closure` · `check:eager-locale-catalogues` · `check-changeset-presence` · `check-governed-queue-guard --test` (not a governed surface).

The **performance-budget** workflow reaches this diff. Read in full: it pins `MAX_ENTRY_GZIP_KB=350` against `index-*.js` only, selected by `find ... -name 'index-*.js'`. It never measures CSS, so no pinned number moves. `check:eager-closure` passes unchanged.
